# Polyfills on Druid

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_polyfill_docs.py from provisa/transpiler/polyfill: do not edit by hand. -->

A polyfill is how Provisa gives a PostgreSQL client PostgreSQL's behaviour on Druid (dialect `druid`), as a serving engine or as a source a statement is sent to directly. Each feature has a read polyfill, how its values and operations are computed there, and a write polyfill, how its values reach it; each states its limitations.

This page lists every feature that has a polyfill or a limitation on Druid. A feature Druid does natively with no difference from PostgreSQL is left out: 1 of the grid's 12 features are left out as native. The conformance runs check the omission: a feature left out that answers otherwise than PostgreSQL fails the run.

When Druid is a serving engine reading a source it attaches directly, it may push work into that source, with the source's semantics, so a result can depend on the pair; the cases known are fixed by hints, listed under each source.

Rules on this page: 12, of which 0 are only the name of a rewrite function. A rule is printed as the translator runs it: the PostgreSQL pattern, its holes written `$name` (typed with `::type`), then the dialect's replacement.
